claims.text: A tailored heat treatment will induce a coherent nanoprecipitate network in the high-entropy alloy intermediate layer.
The coherent nanoprecipitate network will enhance heat-transfer capability.
The heat-treated intermediate layer will preserve structural integrity under plasma-reactor conditions.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers exhibit excellent mechanical strength.
Current high-entropy-alloy intermediate layers have suboptimal thermal conductivity.
An optimized thermal treatment can control coherent nanoprecipitate formation in the alloy microstructure.
Plasma-facing reactor components experience high temperatures and high heat flux.
The relevant operating environment includes mechanical loading, thermal cycling, and transient high heat loads.
The treatment will produce a well-spaced and coherent nanoprecipitate morphology.
The nanoprecipitate network will form continuous pathways for phonon transport through the alloy matrix.
Improved connectivity of phonon-conduction paths will increase thermal conductivity.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces will prevent the treatment from compromising mechanical integrity.
The modified alloy will exhibit a significant increase in effective thermal conductivity relative to conventionally treated material.
The modified alloy will retain high-temperature strength.
The modified alloy will retain resistance to thermal shock.
The limited heat-transfer performance of the baseline layers is caused by a less optimized microstructure.
The proposed benefits may not manifest outside extreme plasma-reactor thermal and mechanical conditions.
The exact thermal-conductivity enhancement and optimal precipitate size, spacing, and volume fraction are not established.
The controlled experiment compares conventionally heat-treated samples with samples receiving the tailored heat treatment under the same simulated reactor conditions.
Failure to exceed a 20% thermal-conductivity improvement, or any measurable degradation of mechanical properties, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
